summary: The article accurately describes SEBI's proposed MF-only PMS framework, including the investment threshold, fee structure, and target audience, based on recent consultation papers.

claims.claim: SEBI has proposed a new category of Portfolio Management Services (PMS) that will exclusively invest in mutual funds.
claims.note: SEBI released a consultation paper on July 23, 2026, proposing an MF-only PMS framework.

claims.claim: The entry threshold for this new service is set at a more accessible ₹25 lakhs, significantly lower than traditional PMS.
claims.note: The proposed minimum investment for MF-only PMS is ₹25 lakhs, compared to ₹50 lakhs for traditional PMS.

claims.claim: Traditional PMS typically requires a minimum investment of ₹50 lakhs, making it accessible primarily to high-net-worth individuals (HNIs).
claims.note: SEBI mandates a ₹50 lakh minimum investment for traditional PMS.

claims.claim: For MF-only PMS, investors will effectively be paying two layers of fees: the PMS management fee charged by the portfolio manager and the expense ratio of the underlying mutual funds they invest in.
claims.note: The article correctly identifies the layered fee structure.

claims.claim: Under the proposal, portfolio managers operating under MF-only PMS can charge a fixed management fee capped at 2.5% of assets under management (AUM).
claims.note: The proposed fixed management fee for MF-only PMS is capped at 2.5% of AUM.

claims.claim: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), especially those based in the Gulf, are typically eligible to invest in SEBI-regulated investment products like PMS, subject to specific regulatory guidelines and KYC requirements.
claims.note: NRIs are generally eligible to invest in PMS, with the new MF-only PMS also being relevant for them.

article_title: SEBI's New MF-Only PMS: A ₹25 Lakh Gateway to Managed Funds
